items.body_html: the start mode, every modes: tag, and default_mode all name a mode in template.modes; tags are allowed only on the two supported surfaces (a gate binding, a *_ref) — elsewhere is mode_tag_on_unsupported_surface; a mono-mode template (empty modes) carries no mode surface. Same fail-closed discipline as slots
apply_mode prunes gate bindings and context refs into a pinned, mode-specific definition; the kernel reads that definition and never branches on the mode at runtime — there is no runtime mode field

items.name_html: mode is not a gate input
items.body_html: the kernel passes no mode to a gate evaluator. Mode resolution decides which binding survives; mode-specific behavior comes from the surviving binding's config (two bindings, same uses, different config) — not from the policy inspecting the mode. One source of truth, no hidden runtime mode dependency

items.name_html: docs-only is an explicit gate, not gate-absence
items.body_html: the doc variant does not merely drop the runtime-validation gate — it keeps a docs_only_runtime_evidence gate whose allow result produces durable evidence for the intended trusted-skip and records its ref on the GateDecision (LC1 INV-3). Removing a gate alone would not say "this skip is intended & trusted"; the explicit doc gate does

surface 2 prunes only the contribution / ref (a *_refs entry); the shared catalog context_blocks entry always stays — a mode-tagged catalog block would leave dangling refs (the L2b render-by-ref hazard)
